Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No operational centralized government portal with national ID authentication was found as of early 2026. DPI Map records: 'Enables authentication via government portal: NA.' The Ministry of Interior website (macnibe.interieur.gov.dz and passeport.interieur.gov.dz) allows tracking of biometric document applications but does not function as a general government SSO portal. The November 2025 draft law on digital identity aims to create a national digital ID platform linked to biometric cards for e-government access, but this had not yet been enacted or deployed.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are not publicly available. DPI Map records: 'Terms of data storage and sharing available: NO' and 'Data handling terms exist: NO'. While Law 18-07 (as amended by Law 25-11 in 2025) requires ANPDP declarations and processing records, no publicly documented data sharing framework, consent mechanisms, or data flow documentation specific to the CNIBE system was found. Searched DPI Map, Ministry of Interior website, ANPDP website, and Algerian legal databases.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No specific digital ID regulation exists as of early 2026. DPI Map explicitly records: 'Regulation for digital ID: NO'. The existing CNIBE is governed by general identity legislation (Presidential Decree 17-143 of 2017) rather than a dedicated digital ID law. The November 2025 cabinet-approved draft law on digital identity and trust services would be the first such specific regulation, but it had not yet been enacted by the legislature as of the research date. Searched DPI Map, government sources, and official Algerian legislation databases.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNIBE is widely accepted as proof of identity in practice (required for voting, banking, administrative services, and obtaining a certificate of nationality per Ministry of Justice guidance of March 2025). However, the DPI Map records 'Identity act codifies legal status: NO', meaning the identity legislation does not explicitly codify the digital/biometric card as having equivalent legal status to traditional proof of identity. The November 2025 draft law would grant electronic documents the same legal validity, but it had not been enacted. Searched DPI Map, identity legislation, and Algerian legal databases.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No publicly documented regular security audits or independent third-party assessments specifically of the CNIBE system were found. Presidential Decree No. 26-07 of 7 January 2026 established a new cybersecurity framework mandating dedicated cybersecurity units in all public institutions with continuous monitoring and regular audits, but this is a new framework and its application to the CNIBE has not been publicly reported. In 2024, Algeria recorded over 70 million cyberattacks (Kaspersky). No independent security audit reports of the national ID system have been published. Searched government websites, security reports, and audit publications.
